questions.text: An overnight reporting query aggregating monthly active users across three years has slowed drastically due to data skew on customer account IDs. How would you diagnose the skew and optimize the query execution in a cloud data warehouse?
questions.question: An overnight reporting query aggregating monthly active users across three years has slowed drastically due to data skew on customer account IDs. How would you diagnose the skew and optimize the query execution in a cloud data warehouse?
key_points: Inspect query profile or execution plan to identify skewed stages and imbalanced spill-to-disk
Repartition or salt high-cardinality join keys to distribute data across worker nodes evenly
Pre-aggregate intermediate account metrics using daily summary rollups or materialized views
Evaluate columnar warehouse sorting and clustering keys on timestamp and account columns

questions.text: You need to compute rolling 7-day active user retention from a raw event log table where users trigger multiple events per day. How would you structure a SQL query using window functions to calculate this metric accurately?
questions.question: You need to compute rolling 7-day active user retention from a raw event log table where users trigger multiple events per day. How would you structure a SQL query using window functions to calculate this metric accurately?
key_points: Deduplicate events by user and calendar day using a CTE or subquery
Apply window functions with framing (ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
Join daily activity back to user cohort acquisition dates
Ensure event timestamp columns are indexed or partitioned by date for scanning efficiency

questions.text: What is the primary difference between a star schema and a snowflake schema in an analytical data warehouse?
questions.question: What is the primary difference between a star schema and a snowflake schema in an analytical data warehouse?
key_points: Star schema uses denormalized dimension tables directly connected to the central fact table
Snowflake schema normalizes dimension tables into secondary lookup hierarchies
Star schemas offer faster query performance with fewer joins; snowflake schemas reduce redundancy
questions.rationale: Tests Data Modeling under SQL & Warehousing: required skill (15% role weighting), to probe candidate gap. Calibrated at easy difficulty.

questions.text: An executive dashboard showing daily revenue trends fluctuates wildly due to weekend seasonality and payment gateway batching. What visualization technique would you use to reveal true underlying trends without misleading stakeholders?
questions.question: An executive dashboard showing daily revenue trends fluctuates wildly due to weekend seasonality and payment gateway batching. What visualization technique would you use to reveal true underlying trends without misleading stakeholders?
key_points: Overlay a 7-day or 30-day moving average trendline over raw daily bar or line metrics
Include week-over-week or trailing-twelve-months comparison benchmarks
Clearly annotate data ingestion lags or batch processing windows
Provide interactive tooltips breaking down revenue by payment processor or region

questions.text: A product manager insists that a recent feature drop increased user engagement, but your regression analysis indicates the metric lift is statistically insignificant. How would you communicate these findings to convince the product team to reconsider?
questions.question: A product manager insists that a recent feature drop increased user engagement, but your regression analysis indicates the metric lift is statistically insignificant. How would you communicate these findings to convince the product team to reconsider?
key_points: Present the data visually with confidence intervals rather than abstract statistical jargon
Frame the insight around business impact, opportunity costs, and risk of false attribution
Propose a controlled A/B test or extended observation period to gather conclusive evidence
Acknowledge product goals while guiding the team toward decisions supported by data
